To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
UV irradiation is the most effective method for degradation of the studied phenylurea pesticides.
the combination of UV-photolysis with TiO2-catalysis and/or ozone addition is the most efficient procedure for the decomposition of the investigated phenylurea compounds.

UV photolyses, ozone, TiO2 photocatalysis and combined processes are suitable for the decomposition of phenylureas, but heterogeneous photocatalysis is the most effective method in the mineralization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the comparison of various AOPs in terms of their applicability for the degradation of chlorinated pesticides.
the degradation of phenyurea herbicides by various advanced oxidation processes (UV photolysis, ozone, heterogeneous photocatalysts and their combinations).
the development of a new method for the degradation of pesticides in water, based on the combined action of UV irradiation, ozone, and heterogeneous photocatalysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
UV photolyses are suitable for the treatment of diuron, while ozonation is the most efficient procedure for fenuron.
UV photolyses and ozonation are the best methods for degradation of the investigated phenylurea pesticides.
the combination of ozone with UV photolysis and/or heterogeneous photocatalysis is the best choice in the degradation of phenyurea herbicides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
UV-ozonation was the best procedure for the degradation of the phenyl ureas.
the combination of ozonation with UV photolysis and/or heterogeneous photocatalysis can be considered as the most efficient method in the removal of phenylureas from water.
UV-photolysis is suitable for the removal of the most toxic and persistent intermediates and ozonation can be used for the removal of less toxic and more labile intermediates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of UV-ozonation and UV-TiO2 photocatalysis is a very efficient procedure for the degradation of the phenylures and their intermediates.
UV photolyses of diuron and ozonation of fenuron are suitable for the removal of these pesticides in water.
the combination of AOPs can be a useful tool in the treatment of complex wastewater containing various pollutants, such as pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and personal care products.
